newsitem.title: USA: Hoffman-La Roche trial of transplant drug positive.
newsitem.headline: Hoffman-La Roche trial of transplant drug positive.

text.p: Hoffmann-La Roche Inc and Protein Design Labs Inc said Tuesday that patients treated with Zenapax in two Phase III trials showed improvement in mortality and graft survival six months after transplants.
Based on the results, Hoffmann-La Roche said it would file in the first half of 1997 for marketing clearance for Zenapax to be used in kidney transplants in the United States, Canada and Europe.

"These results build on our earlier findings that Zenapax was effective in reducing the incidence of acute rejection episodes, which may contribute to graft survival and improvement in patient outcome," the companies said in a release.

The latest studies included 535 patients, half of whom received Zenapax. The companies said there was one death within six months of transplant among patients receiving Zenapax, compared with 10 deaths among patients who did not receive the drug. Patient mortality at six months was 0.4 percent in Zenapax-treated patients and 3.7 percent in patients not receiving Zenapax. Graft loss at six months was 6.0 percent in Zenapax-treated patients and 11.6 percent in patients not receiving Zenapax.
If approved by regulatory authorities, Hoffmann-La Roche will market Zenapax worldwide and pay royalties to Protein Design based on sales, the companies said.
Hoffmann-La Roche is part of Roche Holding Ltd.
